description: Orbitrix builds AstroVitals - an AI astronaut health guardian. A live ESP32 wearable streams vitals with offline buffering. Models trained on NASA OSDR I4, LSDA Bedrest, HRP Roadmap, and ESA COGNISPACE give explainable risk scores. Neuro-Shield adds cognitive testing. Seeking hardware, ML, frontend, and design teammates.
summary:
We developed AstroVitals Neuro-Shield, a closed-loop astronaut health monitoring and autonomous clinical decision support platform built for deep-space exploration. It integrates a custom ESP32-WROOM-32 biometric wearable (MAX30102 pulse oximeter, DS18B20 skin temperature sensor, MPU-6050 6-axis motion tracker, OLED HUD, and haptic alerts) with a React 19 cockpit dashboard, a deterministic Python scientific engine, and an AI clinical companion named Ori.

It directly addresses Challenge 5 (Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts) by fusing real-time wearable telemetry with regularized machine learning models trained on 299 longitudinal samples across 36 human subjects harmonized from NASA OSDR Inspiration4, NASA Twin Study, NASA HRP Bed Rest, and ESA Concordia datasets. Enforcing a strict 'Layer Rule', all HRV metrics, trend tests, and NASA-STD-3001 radiation dosages run in pure deterministic Python while Ori prescribes verified NASA Human Research Program (HRP) countermeasures with zero arithmetic hallucination.

This is vital because on missions to the Moon and Mars, communication delays of up to 22 minutes one-way make real-time Earth telemedicine impossible during acute medical emergencies. AstroVitals operates 100% offline ('OFFLINE=1'), empowering crews with immediate, flight-surgeon-grade medical autonomy in signal-denied deep space.
details:
What AstroVitals Does & How It Works:

AstroVitals Neuro-Shield is a closed-loop astronaut health monitoring and autonomous clinical decision support system for Challenge 5 (Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts). It enforces a strict 5-layer architecture where the LLM never performs arithmetic:

1. Wearable Telemetry Hub (Hardware): An ESP32-WROOM-32 biometric wearable captures real-time PPG heart rate and SpO2 (MAX30102), digital skin temperature (DS18B20), and 6-axis motion (MPU-6050). Using acceleration vectors (above 0.25 g), firmware performs edge motion-artifact rejection, displays metrics on an SSD1306 OLED HUD, and triggers instant 5-pulse haptic vibration and LED alerts if vitals breach safety envelopes (HR below 40 or above 180 BPM, SpO2 below 90%, Temp below 35.0 C or above 39.0 C), even during total Wi-Fi blackouts.

2. Deterministic Scientific Engine (Compute): All calculations run in pure Python, NumPy, and SciPy ('backend/compute/'). It computes HRV (RMSSD, SDNN), Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) z-scores, Mann-Kendall trend tests, Theil-Sen slopes, and NASA-STD-3001 cumulative radiation dosages (600 mSv career and 250 mSv SPE limits, with a 10x dose multiplier over the South Atlantic Anomaly).

3. Harmonized Spaceflight ML Models: To solve small-N overfitting without mixing Earth ICU datasets, we harmonized 299 longitudinal samples across 36 human subjects from four cohorts: NASA OSDR Inspiration4 ('OSD-569' to 'OSD-575'), NASA Twin Study ('OSD-294'), NASA HRP 70-Day Bed Rest ('OSD-379'), and ESA Concordia ('ESA-ICE-CONCORDIA'). Validated via zero-leakage 5-fold GroupKFold by 'subject_id':

- Cardiovascular Risk (BayesianRidge): CV R2 = 0.673 (MAE 5.34)

- Immune Risk (BayesianRidge): CV R2 = 0.670 (MAE 5.15)

- Sleep/Circadian Risk (VotingRegressor): CV R2 = 0.577 (MAE 6.49)

- Frontline Anomaly Sentinel: Unsupervised IsolationForest for real-time outlier detection.

4. Grounded AI Companion (Ori) & MCP Server: Powered by Gemini 1.5 Flash and a custom FastMCP server ('mcp_server.py'), Ori uses 5 deterministic tools ('vitals_anomaly_check', 'trend_test', 'osdr_search', 'ntrs_search', 'cite_check') to interpret pre-computed trends, cite NASA NTRS literature, and prescribe NASA HRP countermeasures.

5. Offline-First HUD & Provenance Gate: Built with React 19 and FastAPI, AstroVitals runs 100% offline ('OFFLINE=1') via a 'Live -> Cache -> Fixture' fallback and SSE stream replay. Every metric shows a Provenance Badge ('LIVE NOAA', 'CACHE', 'FIXTURE') opening a drawer with verified NASA dataset IDs and URLs validated by 'cite_check()'.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

On Moon and Mars missions, up to 22-minute one-way communication delays make live Earth telemedicine impossible during acute arrhythmias, hypoxia, or radiation storms. AstroVitals delivers autonomous flight-surgeon triage aboard the spacecraft and provides a blueprint for remote rural and disaster-zone telemedicine on Earth.

Creativity & Factors Considered (Cost, Energy, Accessibility):

- Creativity: Strict 'Layer Rule' separating Python math from LLM narration; cross-cohort biomarker ratios ('NLR', 'BUN_to_Creatinine', 'Inflammation_Index', 'CardioMetabolic_Ratio'); hardware motion-artifact freezing; Digital Twin and Neuro-Shield cognitive testing.

- Cost & Energy: Built with off-the-shelf hardware under $25 USD, low-power ESP32 telemetry, and lightweight regularized linear models requiring minimal compute.

- Accessibility: High-contrast cockpit UI, multi-sensory alerts (LEDs, OLED, and tactile vibrations), and open-source Apache-2.0 licensing.

Tools, Hardware & Software:

- Hardware: ESP32-WROOM-32, MAX30102, DS18B20, MPU-6050, SSD1306 OLED, 2N2222 haptic driver, C++/PlatformIO.

- Software: Python, FastAPI, Scikit-Learn, SciPy, NumPy, SQLite, Firebase, React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS, FastMCP, Gemini 1.5 Flash.

- Links: Web App (https://astrovitals.vercel.app) | API (https://astrovitals.onrender.com/docs) | GitHub (https://github.com/TanvirAhmmedCodes/AstroVitals).

AI/SI Disclosure:

Team Orbitrix designed the architecture, hardware, biomarker engineering, and validation. Google Antigravity IDE (Gemini) assisted with code scaffolding and documentation, and Gemini 1.5 Flash powers Ori for grounded explanation without arithmetic ('docs/AI_USE.md').
